text:
maya: Heads up — staging perf alert after yesterday's model bump (checkpoint v2.4.1). p99 token latency jumped ~2.1x on long-tail prompts, throughput oscillating. link to dashboard: https://internal.redwood/staging/perf/2020 :grimacing:
liam: seeing same locally with a small repro, batch sizes keep flipping between 1 and 8 every few seconds, looks like batching heuristic oscillation.
sasha: do we have a profiler capture? sounds like kernel route churn or alloc thrash.
maya: uploaded a capture to S3: s3://redwood-staging/profiles/2020/bump-v241/ — key bits pasted below.
liam: Small flame snippet:
```
kernel_select: llm_attn_v2 -> fallback_kernel_v1  (80% -> 45% over 30s)
kv_cache_evictions/sec: 180 -> 900
avg_batch_size: 7.9 -> 2.3
mem_rss: 35GB -> 52GB (spikes)
```
anton: Oof. Kernel selector seems to be flipping mid-request depending on seq-len distribution. If tokenizer changed padding/eos it's plausible.
sasha: Which commits in the merge? I can start a bisect across the last release train.
maya: Suspect set: tokenizer PR #468, batch-heuristics #472, kernel-fallback tuning #474. All merged in the same window.
ci-bot: perf-e2e/staging reported regression on 2020-11-02. p50 +8%, p95 +44%, p99 +110%. Full run: https://ci.redwood/runs/9682
liam: Quick repro command I used: `./bin/infer --model checkpoint:v2.4.1 --prompt-file tests/long_prompts.txt --concurrency 32 --profile`
liam: When I forced padding to minimal (trim right) the oscillation stops and avg batch jumps back up.
sasha: That points to tokenizer padding to fixed multiple change. Maya — can you confirm what tokenizer config changed in #468?
maya: #468 updated pad_to_multiple_of: 64 -> 128 for some safety with quant kernels. Also changed eos-handling to emit explicit EOS token for a subset of prompts.
anton: pad_to_multiple_of doubling would increase effective sequence lengths for many short prompts — triggers different kernel path (qkv tiling) and increases kv cache pressure.
liam: I ran a quick run with the old tokenizer config and v2.4.1 model binary; perf returned to baseline. So it's config drift, not the checkpoint itself.
sasha: Good catch. We should revert the tokenizer config change in staging and re-run canary.
maya: I'll roll a hotfix revert for tokenizer config (revert commit 9f3a2d). Planning a staging deploy in 10m. ops-bot: queued rollback job #RL-332, ETA 10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ci-bot: note — downstream perf tests will still show delta until kernels warm back up; we should run 30m sustained.
liam: Also propose adding a guard in the routing layer: if avg_batch_size < 3 for > 10s, favor stable kernel route (avoid flip). Less risky than changing heuristics immediately.
anton: Agree. We should also add a regression test in CI: a synthetic workload with many short prompts + pad multiple config to catch future changes.
maya: After revert deploy: staging p99 back within 7% of baseline after 12m, avg_batch_size stabilized at ~7.6. KV evictions dropped to normal.
sasha: Great. Next steps: 1) revert landed and canary; 2) add CI perf test for pad_to_multiple_of combos (sasha/anton); 3) add routing guard (liam); 4) follow-up to consider kernel selector hysteresis (maya).
anton: I'll file a follow-up RFC for selector hysteresis and safe thresholds.
liam: I'll pick up the routing guard PR and include an opt-in flag for canary.
maya: Thanks all. Posting root cause summary to #postmortems once we finish the CI test and RFC.
ops-bot: rollback RL-332 completed, deploy id de-55a3, check https://deploys.redwood/55a3
ci-bot: perf-e2e/staging rerun finished: p99 delta now +6% (within acceptable). Marking run 9682-fixed.
maya: Closing loop — root cause: tokenizer config drift (pad_to_multiple_of increase + eos emission change) triggered longer effective seqs -> kernel selection flip -> batch oscillation -> KV cache thrash. Mitigations: revert + routing guard + CI test + selector hysteresis RFC. :white_check_mark:
